title: Application Route
description: The path a particular applicant uses to apply for a particular Opportunity in a particular intake. One Opportunity can have several routes — central, direct, international, special-category — with different rounds, fees and deadlines. This is why a single 'apply here' link on an institution is not good enough.

appliesTo.description: Opportunity ids. Empty means it applies to every Opportunity in the destination.

readerAccess.description: Whether this site’s reader can take this route at all. A closed route renders once, exclusion first, with no date to act on; its rounds and milestones inherit it.

choicesRanked.description: Where true, ordering changes the outcome and the student needs telling.

dateState.description: Why there is no date, when there is none. A researched finding — "there is no central deadline", "each institution sets its own" — is not a missing value, and a milestone that cannot say which it is renders as "Date not published", which is a lie about work that was done. Mirrors the states a country profile deadline may declare; src/lib/publication-floor.mjs holds the list and src/lib/calendar.mjs reads it.

provisional.description: True when the round's closing date is not confirmed for this cycle (inherited, or its source gives no year). A provisional date must never be shown as a confirmed one.

milestones.description: Dated events, not only deadlines. Opening, result, reply and deposit dates all matter.

timeOfDay.description: Kept because 12:00 and 23:59 are very different promises.

provisional.description: True when inherited from a previous cycle. A provisional date must never be shown as a confirmed one.

supersedes.description: "<routeId>/<milestoneId>" of a general date this one replaces wherever this one is shown. An institution's own date for a step the route also dates in general (TU Delft's 1 April beside the national 1 May, SDU's 3 August beside the earliest-known reply date): on that institution's pages the general date is left out, because two dates for one step leave a student to guess which binds. src/lib/school-dates.mjs reads it; the calendar keeps both.

ibCalendar.description: "<session>/<event>" in data/ib-calendar.json, e.g. "2027-05/results-day". Present when this milestone's date is the IB's rather than this Destination's. IB results day was one fact written into 41 files, twenty-two of them with the identical label, and it had already drifted; scripts/test-ib-calendar.mjs refuses a milestone that states an IB date without this pointer, and refuses a date that disagrees with the record it points at.

Mirrors the states a country profile deadline may declare; src/lib/publication-floor.mjs holds the list and src/lib/calendar.mjs reads it.

destinationOfItem.description: Where it actually has to arrive — often not the portal.

jurisdiction.description: The Application Jurisdiction(s) this route serves, where the Destination declares several. One id, or an array where a route genuinely serves more than one — Canada’s apply-direct route covers Quebec, Alberta and Nova Scotia, and forcing that to be unscoped made it the destination-wide fallback, which is exactly what the route floor check exists to catch. A route with no jurisdiction and no appliesTo covers the whole Destination: the right shape for a centralised system and the wrong one for a federal one.
